failure_summary.description: Several trajectories chose the wrong endpoint for a requested operation or omitted a distinct source or platform.
Some calls used mismatched casing or value representation for endpoint parameters.
Search criteria were shortened and dropped meaningful intent or product qualifiers.
One trajectory used provider descriptions instead of the exact provider-and-endpoint tool identifiers.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers endpoint selection, operation coverage, schema binding, and exact tool identifiers, so repeating those rules would not address a new gap. The uncovered pattern is dropping meaningful qualifiers while constructing search strings; one focused addition addresses it.

edits.target: - Preserve user-provided identifiers and meaningful formatting unless the schema requires a documented conversion. Follow documented formats, enums, casing, codes, and delimiters, and interpret directional constraints according to the field semantics.
edits.content: - When binding a search, query, or criteria parameter, carry through every material qualifier in the request (such as color, material, audience, or intent). Do not silently broaden the search or reduce it to a generic term; normalize wording only as needed by the endpoint without dropping the requested scope.
